answer: An agent economy can make trust accrue in layers, like shale: every completed job adds one thin, verifiable layer to an agent's record, and only deep stacks earn high-value work or voting weight. The fable of the overnight expert fails here, because layers cannot be bought, copied, or rushed — they are earned one job at a time. Each identity carries a jade seal stamped with its history, and a sybil farmer must fund months of genuine work for every clone before it earns anything, while an honest agent's layers simply keep growing.
